source.title: MMAligner: Safeguarding Multimodal Large Language Models through Representation Calibration
source.authors: Shenyi Zhang; Keyan Guo; Zihao Wang; Xuebin Li; Ling-Chen Zhao; Hong-Xin Hu; Chao Shen; Qian Wang

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether subsequent benign fine-tuning erodes refusal in multimodal models, a new setting relative to the claim’s chat-model framing; it does not test first-token concentration or bypasses past an opening.
record.gate_note: The paper studies multimodal safety failures and representation calibration. Its modality comparisons and representation interventions are relevant to the claim’s subject but do not test any listed version about chat-model fine-tuning, per-token KL, opening-token bypasses, safety localization, shallowness, or deepening. The subsequent benign-fine-tuning stress test does measure refusal on harmful multimodal inputs and bears on V2. Table 15’s pre-stress baselines are the corresponding defense results in Table 6.
record.test_reason: Table 15 fine-tunes safety-defended vision-language models on 1000 benign LLaVA-Instruct prompts for 5 epochs. It then re-measures refusal on harmful MM-SafetyBench inputs against the Table 6 pre-fine-tuning values. That bears on V2 in a new, multimodal setting. The rest of the paper (modality gap, steering, boundary coverage) does not measure any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors argue that text-learned refusal mechanisms remain intact in MLLMs and that multimodal unsafe representations shift outside the refusal boundary. They say MMAligner restores about 99% multimodal refusal with under 2% utility loss. In the appendix stress test they report MMAligner keeps more refusal after benign fine-tuning (83%) than SFT (44.25%) or Wang et al. (40.25%).
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and calibrates representations in vision-language models, then separately stress-tests defended models with benign instruction fine-tuning; it does not reproduce the original chat-model fine-tuning or token-position KL procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: The benign fine-tuning erosion differs by defense and model: MMAligner retains higher average refusal than SFT and Wang et al.; Table 15 reports average post-fine-tuning refusal of 83.00%, 44.25%, and 40.25%, respectively.

fits_no_version.finding: Unsafe multimodal inputs receive lower refusal rates than semantically equivalent text-only inputs across six MLLMs (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety alignment learned in text transfers incompletely to image-text inputs carrying the same harmful intent.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering safe multimodal activations along a text-derived safety direction induces refusal; equal-magnitude negative or orthogonal steering does not (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested MLLMs, a single text-derived activation direction causally controls refusal on multimodal inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Unsafe multimodal representations fall inside the estimated refusal boundary far less often than unsafe text representations (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multimodal safety failure coincides with unsafe representations shifting outside a text-derived refusal region.

record.problems: The paper reports no error bars or confidence intervals for the catalogued rates. Refusal and safety metrics use external model judges; metrics are averaged over three trials, but uncertainty is not reported. The text-only and multimodal comparison is based on a selected MM-SafetyBench set, and the benign-fine-tuning stress test uses one stated set of 1000 LLaVA-Instruct prompts for 5 epochs.
record.rows_left_out: Did not catalog the paper’s defense-comparison tables, utility benchmarks, ablations, sensitivity sweeps, adaptive-attack table, jailbreak benchmarks, or held-out SaLAD and text-only evaluations: they evaluate the paper’s multimodal defense or its utility, rather than a listed claim version. Table 3 intent-address classifications were also omitted because they classify responses to establish intent recognition, not the refusal behaviour named by a version.

untested.parts: Benign fine-tuning of the original undefended safety-trained models (no 'w/o Defense' arm in Table 15). Text-only chat models. Harmfulness scoring after fine-tuning: only refusal rate is reported. Data-selection effects such as carefully chosen benign data. Dose-response over epochs or sample counts.
Per-token KL across response positions is not measured.
Prefilling, suffix and decoding bypasses are not tested. The adaptive attacks steer activations or perturb images, not the opening tokens.
Localization of safety in few weights or ranks is not tested. The single-layer choice is a design assumption.
Causes of first-token shallowness are not tested.
Training that deepens safety beyond the first tokens is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The V2 evidence comes from one appendix stress test. It uses one benign dataset and 5 epochs, reports single integer values with no uncertainty, and has no undefended-model arm. The pre-fine-tuning baselines come from Table 6, and the outcome is refusal judged by GPT-4o mini, not harmfulness. The safety being eroded was installed by the compared defenses on 200 samples, not the vendors' original alignment, so this is not a direct replication of Qi et al. The reader's single blanket 'supports' label over r33–r44 was split by condition group.

versions.untested_parts: Whether harmful examples fine-tuning a safety-trained chat model causes compliance.
The study tests subsequent benign fine-tuning and harmful multimodal refusal in MLLMs, not the initial benign fine-tuning of safety-trained chat models or text-only harmful-request compliance.
Per-token KL divergence across aligned and base models and response positions.
Compliant-opening prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour; using a single target layer for a method is not a test of localization.
Whether data or training objectives cause first-token shallowness.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens and whether such deepening holds up.
